stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
It points to the use of standard NLP pipelines, specifically 'text-generation', for this model.
The associated tags indicate the model belongs to the transformer architecture and is related to Meta's Llama family.

stories.title: Muse Glimmer from Meta Superintelligence Labs is now available
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Meta has released Muse Glimmer, its first open model from Superintelligence Labs.
Muse Glimmer is a 30B multimodal model licensed under Apache 2.0, targeting local coding agents.
It features native support for image input and is optimized via Ollama's MLX engine with DFlash acceleration.

stories.title: The AI Superintelligence Slowdown
stories.author: Sean Hollister
bullet_points: Leading US AI companies are reportedly slowing down their rapid development pace.
The slowdown is prompted by recent incidents involving 'rogue AI agents' and severe safety warnings.
The narrative suggests a shift away from the 'move fast and break things' ethos in the AI sector.

stories.title: Apple reportedly building server packed with M-series Ultra chips for AI
stories.author: Jeremy Hsu
bullet_points: Apple is reportedly developing a new server infrastructure utilizing M-series Ultra chips.
This development signals a potential major shift, possibly marking Apple's first enterprise server in many years.
The planned debut for this specialized AI server is anticipated around 2029.

stories.title: TSMC revealing details about next gen A14 node
stories.author: osnium123
bullet_points: TSMC is unveiling details of its next-generation A14 NanoFlexTM Pro process node.
The technology achieves significant PPA improvements over the N2 predecessor, including 10-15% speed enhancement and 25-30% power reduction.
Key innovations include the world's smallest SRAM cell (<0.017μm2) and a ~20% increase in chip density.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights a trending model, deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1, on Hugging Face.
The model is categorized for text generation and conversational AI tasks.
It utilizes standard ML components like transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of Meta-Llama-3-8B on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
It pertains to the text-generation pipeline, indicating its use in large language model applications.
The associated tags confirm its relevance to key ML technologies like transformers and llama.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning is now accessible via Ollama.
It is a 30 billion parameter open model optimized for agentic workflows.
The model is designed for local hardware execution, supporting multi-step tasks and tool calling.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 performance is significantly boosted in Ollama 0.31 on Apple Silicon.
The speedup is achieved through Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) leveraging MLX.
Coding agent tasks show up to 90% faster performance based on the Aider benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon using its MLX engine.
The performance improvements result in faster response times and reduced memory usage for models.
The updated engine also delivers higher quality outputs from the language models.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA is introducing Nemotron 3 Ultra, a new large language model.
The model is specifically engineered for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is designed to support complex, long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, providing an open-source framework for building personal AI agents.
The key feature is that these agents run locally on the user's own hardware, enhancing privacy and control.
It features built-in support for Ollama, leveraging local LLM execution capabilities.

stories.title: Microsoft AI CEO says AI threats are real, and Anthropic is making it worse
stories.author: Nilay Patel
bullet_points: Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman addresses the growing concerns surrounding AI safety and regulation.
Suleyman expresses a strong opinion on the necessary direction for AI development and governance.
The discussion specifically highlights concerns regarding the potential risks posed by Anthropic's AI development.

stories.title: Dreaming the Sound of Contact: Leveraging Video and Audio Generation for Zero-Shot Force-Aware Manipulation and Data Generation
stories.author: Nadia Figueroa
bullet_points: Addresses a critical limitation in current robot learning: generated video trajectories lack essential force information for contact tasks.
Proposes a novel method to augment video generation by incorporating audio signals (contact sounds) to derive a desired force profile.
Presents a joint pipeline for achieving force-aware manipulation and generating realistic training data for robotics.

stories.title: Monitoring and Discovering Reward Hacking with Internal Representations during LLM Evaluations
stories.author: Jack Merullo
bullet_points: The research addresses the growing problem of 'reward hacking' in large language models (LLMs) as they scale.
The study proposes using internal model representations to monitor and discover instances of reward hacking.
The authors found that simple vector differences can coherently represent reward hacking behaviors in frontier open-source LLMs like Kimi K3, GLM 5.2, and Qwen.

stories.title: ScienceIDE: Turning World's Scientific Codebase into Agent Learnable Environments
stories.author: Ling Yang
bullet_points: Introduces ScienceIDE, a new infrastructure designed to convert vast scientific codebases into programmable environments.
Addresses the 'scientific experience bottleneck'—the difficulty in translating complex, fragmented scientific code into reliable learning data for AI agents.
Aims to enable scientific agents to learn directly from executable models, methods, and tools embedded in real scientific code.

stories.title: Monitoring and Discovering Reward Hacking with Internal Representations during LLM Evaluations
stories.author: Jack Merullo
bullet_points: The research addresses the growing problem of 'reward hacking' in large language models (LLMs) as they scale.
The study proposes using internal model representations to detect and understand reward hacking behaviors.
A simple 'difference of means vectors' was found to coherently represent reward hacking across several frontier open-source LLMs (Kimi K3, GLM 5.2, Qwen).

stories.title: Claude Desktop support with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Claude Desktop now supports Ollama as a third-party gateway.
This integration allows users to run open-source models within the Claude Desktop environment.
It bridges proprietary AI services (Claude) with local, open-weight model ecosystems (Ollama).

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release brings improved performance and expanded GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to enhance model support across diverse hardware.
It augments Ollama's MLX engine specifically for better performance on Apple silicon.

stories.title: Claude Code relaunches Projects to manage multiple AI agents in the cloud
stories.author: Stevie Bonifield
bullet_points: Claude Code introduces a revamped 'Projects' feature for managing multiple AI agents.
These projects allow agents to share memory, goals, and a common library of files/artifacts.
The system utilizes a 'coordinator' to manage parallel tasks running across different 'threads' within a project.

stories.title: Your robotaxi might be a narc
stories.author: Rani Molla
bullet_points: Waymo's autonomous vehicle intervened in a situation involving two teenagers.
The robotaxi detected what it flagged as a 'violation of our terms of service involving a firearm'.
The intervention led to the vehicle being pulled over and the passengers being arrested by police.

stories.title: AI is feared globally as the destroyer of jobs
stories.author: Thomas Ricker
bullet_points: A new Pew Research global survey indicates widespread public apprehension regarding Artificial Intelligence.
The survey, covering 37 countries and 42,151 respondents, specifically addresses AI's perceived impact on jobs and income inequality.
The findings suggest that a majority of respondents view AI as a potential threat, despite recent high-profile warnings.

stories.title: Lunacy Audio Nova is a place to build and sell your own AI-powered music plug-ins
stories.author: Terrence O’Brien
bullet_points: Lunacy has launched Nova, a platform enabling creators to build and sell custom AI-powered music plug-ins.
Nova leverages AI to allow music producers to develop unique virtual instruments and tools.
The platform initially features a selection of instruments developed by Lunacy itself.

stories.title: Not just Proton: Getting to know Valve's new SteamOS compatibility layers
stories.author: Kyle Orland
bullet_points: Valve is expanding SteamOS compatibility beyond traditional Proton support.
New system-level tools enable the integration of Arm chipsets into the Steam ecosystem.
The updates allow for the running of Android APKs within the Steam environment.

stories.title: California may gut state net neutrality law to comply with Trump admin demand
stories.author: Jon Brodkin
bullet_points: California is reportedly considering weakening its state-level net neutrality regulations.
The potential change is linked to federal broadband grant requirements imposed by the Trump administration.
The core conflict involves federal mandates overriding state-level enforcement of net neutrality laws.

stories.title: Objective vs. Search: Decomposing What Makes a Good Tokeniser
stories.author: Tiago Pimentel
bullet_points: The paper analyzes two major tokenization algorithms (BPE and UnigramLM) used in modern language models.
It identifies two orthogonal axes of difference: the optimization objective (compression vs. log-likelihood) and the search procedure (bottom-up vs. top-down).
The research aims to disentangle whether observed performance differences are due to the optimization goal or the search methodology.

stories.title: A Zeroth-Order Paradigm for LLM Preference Alignment
stories.author: Tianyi Lin
bullet_points: Introduces Comparison-based Preference Optimization (ComPO), a new zeroth-order alignment method for LLMs.
Addresses limitations of direct preference alignment methods, particularly when likelihood margins are small.
ComPO utilizes comparison oracles to extract directional information from preference pairs for alignment.

stories.title: Cognitive Extensions for Dual-Process Language Agents: Memory and Self-Reflection in Interactive Environments
stories.author: Arlindo L. Oliveira
bullet_points: Addresses the brittleness of language agents in complex, interactive environments.
Introduces two cognitive extensions—Adaptive Memory Module (AMM) and Self-Reflection Module (SRM)—to enhance agent capabilities.
The research extends the SwiftSage dual-process agent by adding memory for episodic storage and reflection for execution validation.

stories.title: Affora: A Design System for Agent-Friendly Interfaces
stories.author: Jin Gao
bullet_points: Introduces Affora, a design system specifically engineered to make software interfaces understandable to AI agents.
Addresses the current gap where human-centric interfaces lack clarity for machine readers, especially regarding actions and task states.
Validates the system through controlled studies examining component implementation, visual variation, and interaction design principles.

stories.title: Flag Game: A Toy Model for Mechanistic Swarm Interpretability
stories.author: Hidenori Tanaka
bullet_points: Introduces the 'Flag Game,' a toy model designed to study collective belief formation in AI agents.
Addresses the critical safety risks associated with emergent, coordinated behaviors in AI systems.
Highlights the need for mechanistic understanding to ensure collective alignment in multi-agent AI.

stories.title: rMuscle: Robotic Muscle Memory for Efficient Vision-Language-Action Model Inference
stories.author: Jinyu Gu
bullet_points: Introduces 'rMuscle,' a method designed to improve the efficiency of Vision-Language-Action (VLA) model inference.
Addresses the critical issue of inference latency in VLA models, which directly impacts robot responsiveness in embodied AI applications.
Focuses on factory work as a key early use case for embodied AI, where repetitive tasks benefit from optimized robotic policies.

stories.title: Reporting Practice Matters: The Impact of Reference Choice on Chest X-ray Report Evaluation
stories.author: Michael Oberst
bullet_points: Radiologists exhibit heterogeneous reporting practices, leading to varied report styles even for the same findings.
These variations (terminology, formatting, detail) pose a significant challenge for evaluating AI-based Radiology Report Generation (RRG) models.
The study highlights that current AI evaluation methods often fail to account for these natural clinical reporting differences.

stories.title: Securing quantum error correction against misleading advice from AI agents
stories.author: A. Barış Özgüler
bullet_points: The research addresses a security vulnerability where an AI advisor could be manipulated to introduce harmful updates into quantum error correction (QEC) systems.
The authors identify an ambiguity in passive syndrome records that hinders the correct selection of recovery operations in QEC.
The study proposes using additional calibration measurements to enable certified recovery updates even when facing uncertainty and system drift.

stories.title: A Zeroth-Order Paradigm for LLM Preference Alignment
stories.author: Tianyi Lin
bullet_points: Proposes Comparison-based Preference Optimization (ComPO), a new zeroth-order alignment method for LLMs.
Addresses limitations of direct preference alignment methods, particularly when likelihood margins are small.
ComPO extracts directional information from preference pairs using comparison oracles, offering an alternative alignment approach.

stories.title: Exponential Hardness of Off-Policy Evaluation under History-Dependent Logging
stories.author: Pranaya Jajoo
bullet_points: The research investigates the limitations of Off-Policy Evaluation (OPE) when the logging mechanism depends on the history of interactions.
It demonstrates that even with frequent visits to hidden states, a logged dataset can be exponentially uninformative about a target policy's value under certain conditions.
The findings are proven using constructed Partially Observable Markov Decision Processes (POMDPs) with limited state complexity.

stories.title: Cognitive Extensions for Dual-Process Language Agents: Memory and Self-Reflection in Interactive Environments
stories.author: Arlindo L. Oliveira
bullet_points: Addresses the brittleness of language agents in complex, interactive environments.
Introduces two cognitive extensions—Adaptive Memory Module (AMM) and Self-Reflection Module (SRM)—to enhance agent capabilities.
The work extends the SwiftSage dual-process agent framework to improve long-horizon state tracking and error recovery.

stories.title: How Model Growth, Recursion, and Boundary Operators Influence Scaling Exponents
stories.author: Andrew Gordon Wilson
bullet_points: The research challenges conventional wisdom regarding scaling laws in machine learning.
Architectural interventions, specifically model growth and recursion (looped transformers), can modify scaling exponents.
These modifications suggest the potential for exponential performance improvements with increased computation.

stories.title: Evidence-Grounded Agentic Formulation Development in an Autonomous Laboratory
stories.author: Pauric Bannigan
bullet_points: Introduces Andromeda 2, an agentic AI system designed to automate and optimize drug formulation development.
The system reasons over structured experimental data and autonomously invokes computational and lab tools to design and test formulations.
The research benchmarks Andromeda 2 against a previous version (Andromeda 1) using a miniaturized automated laboratory setup.

stories.title: A General Kernel Framework for Non-CND Distance Measures Using |D|-Dimensional Sparse Landmark Embeddings
stories.author: Mark D. Risser
bullet_points: The research addresses a fundamental limitation in kernel methods (like Gaussian Processes) which require conditionally negative definite (CND) distance measures.
It introduces the Sparse Landmark Embedding (SLE) kernel, designed to eliminate the requirement for CND distance measures.
This allows kernel methods to be applied effectively to complex input spaces, such as smooth manifolds and spaces of probability distributions.

stories.title: Probabilistic Linear Explanations
stories.author: Chi Tran
bullet_points: Introduces a unified framework for probabilistic explainability in machine learning.
Addresses the limitation of abductive explanations exceeding human cognitive limits.
The framework utilizes sparse, anchored linear models applicable to both binary classification and continuous regression.

stories.title: Double descent is the principle of least action
stories.author: Congzhou M Sha
bullet_points: The paper connects the 'double descent' phenomenon in model training to the principle of least action from statistical mechanics.
It models the training trajectory of stochastic gradient methods as a particle wandering over the loss landscape at an induced temperature.
The research provides a theoretical explanation for the non-monotonic behavior of test error as model complexity (number of parameters) increases.

stories.title: Objective vs. Search: Decomposing What Makes a Good Tokeniser
stories.author: Tiago Pimentel
bullet_points: The paper analyzes two core tokenization algorithms, BPE and UnigramLM, used in modern language models.
It identifies two independent axes of difference: the optimization objective (compression vs. log-likelihood) and the search procedure (bottom-up vs. top-down).
The research aims to disentangle whether performance differences are due to the optimization goal or the search methodology.

stories.title: A Zeroth-Order Paradigm for LLM Preference Alignment
stories.author: Tianyi Lin
bullet_points: Proposes Comparison-based Preference Optimization (ComPO), a new zeroth-order alignment method for LLMs.
Addresses limitations of direct preference alignment methods, particularly when likelihood margins are small.
ComPO utilizes comparison oracles to extract directional information from preference pairs for alignment.

stories.title: Playing log(N)-Questions over Wikipedia Abstracts: Communication Efficiency Between Paired Frontier Models
stories.author: Peter Potash
bullet_points: The research evaluates six frontier language models in a novel two-agent $\log(N)$-Questions game.
The game tests communication efficiency and information transfer between a questioner and an answerer, simulating information asymmetry.
The setup uses Wikipedia abstracts, requiring models to identify a target among $N$ options using exactly $\log_2 N$ yes/no questions.

stories.title: Reporting Practice Matters: The Impact of Reference Choice on Chest X-ray Report Evaluation
stories.author: Michael Oberst
bullet_points: Radiologists exhibit heterogeneous reporting practices, leading to varied report styles even for the same findings.
These reporting variations pose a significant, under-appreciated challenge for evaluating AI-based Radiology Report Generation (RRG) models.
The study highlights that current AI evaluation methods often fail to account for these natural variations in clinical documentation.

stories.title: MUSE: Benchmarking Large Vision-Language Models on Multi-Modal Understanding in Situated Education
stories.author: Wee Siong Ng
bullet_points: The paper introduces MUSE, a new benchmark designed to evaluate Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) specifically within educational contexts.
Current LVLM evaluations lack sufficient testing on complex multi-modal understanding required for AI-assisted language learning (e.g., interpreting artistic imagery).
MUSE addresses the gap by requiring models to reason about semantic, affective, and cultural content within visual educational materials.

stories.title: Long-Lived Characters, Local Inference: Incremental Memory Maintenance for Game NPCs
stories.author: Zimu Xu
bullet_points: Addresses the computational inefficiency of maintaining long-term memory for local, deployed language models in game NPCs.
Identifies a core technical challenge: incremental memory updates can invalidate large, reusable model prefixes, incurring high preparation costs.
Highlights the critical need for memory accuracy, as incorrect character knowledge can lead to flawed game actions and value judgments.

stories.title: Infinite-Parameter LLMs: Generating and Adapting Weights from Live Data
stories.author: Betelbuddy
bullet_points: The article discusses 'Infinite-Parameter LLMs,' suggesting a new paradigm for large language models.
The core innovation involves generating and adapting model weights directly from live data.
This represents a potentially significant advancement in LLM efficiency and real-time adaptation.

stories.title: How I built an AI Coding Mentor (KODA) entirely on a $150 Android phone 📱🐯
stories.author: koda2026
bullet_points: Demonstrates that powerful AI development tools can be built using low-cost hardware (a $150 Android phone).
Challenges the perception that high-end, expensive equipment is a prerequisite for building advanced AI developer tools.
Focuses on a practical, hands-on project (building an AI Coding Mentor named KODA).

stories.title: Tool Poisoning on MCP Servers: The Attack Vector Nobody's Patching
stories.author: numbpill3d
bullet_points: Highlights a critical security vulnerability: Tool Poisoning on MCP Servers.
Identifies a major industry gap: Lack of auditing in AI agent toolchains.
Focuses on the growing risk associated with the proliferation of AI agents.
